spillover_issues.author: ravwojdyla-agent
spillover_issues.body:
## Description
Decontamination flags very few documents (~0.01% overall; 0% on arXiv/news). This is **not** a coverage gap and **not** a verbatim-recall failure — it is the recall cost of a deliberately precision-favoring matching design. The question for the team is whether that tradeoff is calibrated where they want it.

### What's confirmed
- Benchmark coverage is comprehensive: 600 families incl. MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval, HellaSwag, GPQA, MATH, DROP, SQuAD, TriviaQA, BBH, AGIEval, …
- Verbatim contamination in a ≥13-word paragraph **is** caught (reproduced a real flagged doc at 0.867 overlap).
- By design, decon (`marin.datakit.decon`) matches 13-word n-grams per paragraph and flags at ≥50% paragraph overlap, and **intentionally ignores paragraphs with <13 words** — the whole-paragraph fallback was removed in #5656 because it produced ~18% phantom contamination from trivial stubs (`"..."`, `"A."`, `"##"`).

### Recall cost of that design (injection test — see comment below)
- **Short-line contamination escapes entirely**: the same contaminated text re-wrapped to 8-word lines → overlap 0.87 → **0.00**. Affects MMLU/ARC options, tables, poetry, any line-broken benchmark text.
- **Embedded contamination is diluted below threshold**: the same paragraph + 1× filler → 0.87 → **0.02**, because overlap is a fraction of the paragraph.

### The decision
Is ~0% flagging the intended operating point — accept missing short-line/embedded leakage in exchange for near-zero false positives — or should recall be raised at the cost of more false positives? If the latter, options that keep the `"..."` artifact suppressed: length-normalize or lower the threshold, add a short-paragraph sliding-window path with a minimum length, or flag on an absolute count of matched n-gram hits rather than the paragraph fraction.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 Update: the decontam benchmark index (`bloom/_combined_10d8e50c/_bloom/eval_hash_index.parquet`) is **comprehensive** — 600 benchmark families, including all standard evals: MMLU (2.2M n-grams), GSM8K, HumanEval, HellaSwag, ARC, GPQA, DROP, MATH, SQuAD, TriviaQA, BBH, AGIEval, Winogrande, PIQA, BoolQ, Lambada (only MBPP absent, and it overlaps HumanEval which is present).

So the near-zero detection is **not** a missing-benchmark problem. Revised hypothesis: either the corpus is genuinely clean (aggressive upstream filtering) or the n-gram overlap threshold is too strict. The injection test in the DoD (inject a known benchmark question, confirm it flags) is the right way to distinguish these.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 Injection test result — the near-zero detection is a **brittle-matching** problem, not coverage. Ran decon's own scoring (`marin.datakit.decon._paragraph_overlap_and_matches`, `NGramConfig(ngram_length=13, stride=0, overlap_threshold=0.5)`) against the production bloom (`bloom/_combined_10d8e50c/_bloom/filter.bin`) using a real flagged corpus doc (guaranteed in the bloom):

- **Verbatim recall works**: reproduced `max_overlap = 0.867` = the stored value → `contaminated = True`. Verbatim benchmark text in a ≥13-word paragraph is caught.
- **Gap 1 — short paragraphs escape entirely**: the *same* contaminated text re-wrapped to 8-word lines → `max_overlap = 0.000`, not flagged. Paragraphs with <13 whitespace tokens produce no n-grams (the whole-paragraph fallback was removed in #5656 to avoid `"..."` false positives). So any benchmark rendered as short lines — MMLU/ARC options, tables, poetry, line-broken text — is invisible to decontam.
- **Gap 2 — embedded contamination is diluted below threshold**: the same contaminated paragraph embedded in filler within one paragraph → `max_overlap = 0.024` (even at 1× filler). Since overlap = matched-13-grams / total-13-grams in the paragraph, any surrounding same-line text pushes it under 0.5.

So the ~0.01% flag rate is neither a clean corpus nor missing benchmarks — it's that real contamination is rarely a standalone paragraph that is ≥50% verbatim benchmark text. Short-line or embedded contamination (the common case) escapes.

Suggested fixes: length-normalize or lower the threshold; add a sliding-window / short-paragraph path (with a min length to avoid the `"..."` artifact); or flag on an absolute count of matched n-gram hits rather than the paragraph fraction.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 Per-source flag-rate sweep over the July-hero store's decon output — quantifies the **precision** side of this tradeoff, and surfaces one large true-positive contamination.

**Method:** resolved `store_8ac06c74` (`s3://marin-us-east-02a/...`) to its 114 per-source decon outputs (`s3://marin-na/marin/datakit/decontam/<source>_<hash>/`, bloom `_combined_e0edd375`) via the web-explorer lineage resolver, then ran ducky over every shard: `count(*)`, `sum(attributes.contaminated)`, and `matched_hashes → eval_hash_index.parquet` joins for eval attribution.

## Corpus-wide it's ~0, but wildly uneven

- **15.09B docs, 5.90M flagged = 0.039% overall** — matches the near-zero headline here.
- But the flag rate is **not** uniformly low. It concentrates almost entirely in sources that share *upstream source material* with benchmarks — **code, books/textbooks, and math** — while web/prose stays at 0. 8 sources flag literally 0 (`nsf_awards`, `svg`, `massive_function_calling`, `economics`, `public_domain_review`, `refuseweb`, …).

Top sources by flag rate:

| source | docs | flagged | flag % |
|---|---|---|---|
| **nemotron_specialized_v1_1/formal_logic** | 489,061 | 172,554 | **35.28%** |
| davinci-dev/ctx-native | 4.16M | 75,825 | 1.82% |
| swe-zero-12m | 12.1M | 200,518 | 1.66% |
| coderforge | 258K | 4,129 | 1.60% |
| cp/oercommons | 5,244 | 81 | 1.54% |
| swe-rebench-openhands | 67K | 981 | 1.46% |
| davinci-dev/env-native | 74K | 1,011 | 1.37% |
| cp/pressbooks | 54K | 695 | 1.28% |
| institutional_books | 983K | 11,173 | 1.14% |
| cp/libretexts | 40K | 433 | 1.08% |
| cp/project_gutenberg | 55K | 544 | 0.98% |
| starcoder2/documentation | 60K | 438 | 0.73% |
| cp/stackv2_code | 218M | 958,972 | 0.44% |
| nemotron_sft/sft_math | 141M | 688,125 | 0.49% |
| nemotron_specialized/math_textbooks | 12.9M | 57,921 | 0.45% |

(prose baseline for contrast: `nsf_awards` 0.00%, web splits ~0.01%.)

## Two distinct phenomena in these flags

**1. False positives from shared source material (the code/book cluster).** Attributed `coderforge`'s flagged docs (1.6% rate) back to evals — dominated not by code-gen benchmarks but by **`code2text_python`** (2,203 docs) and **`code2text_javascript`** (1,256), with only 23 `humaneval` / 50 `livecodebench`. Sampling `code2text_python` directly, its "eval documents" are ordinary public GitHub functions (e.g. `sina_xml_to_url_list`, `dailymotion_download` from the `you-get` repo). Any code corpus containing those popular functions matches them verbatim → flagged. This is **shared open-source code, not test-answer leakage**. Same mechanism drives the books/textbooks cluster (Gutenberg/libretexts/pressbooks/institutional_books match book- and textbook-derived evals like wikitext/lambada/MMLU/MATH). Tail families like `swde`, `mrpc`, `realtoxicityprompts` on code docs are coincidental phrase collisions.

**2. A real, severe true positive.** `nemotron_specialized_v1_1/formal_logic` at **35.28%**: **all 172,554 flagged docs match `mmlu_formal_logic-test`** (and its identical MMLU-Pro / `mmlu_pro_philosophy` duplicates). This isn't an FP — this synthetic source is largely built from / around MMLU formal-logic questions. Decon caught it correctly; the source itself should be dropped or heavily filtered.

So this issue's precision-favoring design does behave as intended on prose, but on code/books it over-removes legitimate shared material, **and** the same run contains at least one source that is genuinely ~35% benchmark contamination.

## Suggested actions

- **Curate the eval set by document type.** Drop benchmarks whose "test documents" are ordinary corpus material — `code2text_*` (CodeXGLUE; public code), and reconsider `wikitext`/`lambada`/`swde` for the book corpora. These drive the bulk of the code + book false positives without weakening real leakage detection.
- **Quantify FP rate before acting:** run `experiments/datakit/decontam/ops/precision_analysis.py` (LLM judge) on `coderforge`, `cp/stackv2_code`, `institutional_books`.
- **Escalate `formal_logic` separately** — 35% MMLU-formal-logic contamination is a source-inclusion problem, not a decon-tuning one.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 **Correction to my previous comment** — I looked at the actual `nemotron_specialized_v1_1/formal_logic` documents and the actual MMLU eval, and the 35.3% is **not** a true positive. It's a **false positive from instruction-template reuse.** The specific questions are novel; only MMLU's fixed instruction boilerplate is shared.

## What I claimed vs. what's there

I earlier wrote that formal_logic's 35% was "real, severe contamination… largely built from/around MMLU formal-logic questions." That's wrong. The flagged docs are **new** formal-logic problems that happen to reuse MMLU's instruction *template*.

## The actual flagged documents (verbatim, from the normalized source)

All three are `max_overlap = 1.0` (a whole paragraph is 100% eval n-grams):

**Doc `0000193367a92858b1835ae8de883bb4`:**
> Construct a complete truth table for the following argument. Then, using the truth table, determine whether the argument is valid or invalid. If the argument is invalid, choose an option which presents a counterexample. (There may be other counterexamples as well.)
> I ≡ (M ∨ O)
> ~R ∨ O
> R / ∴ M ∧ I
> A. Invalid. Counterexample when I is true, M is false, O is true, and R is true
> … Answer: A

**Doc `000054bcaf93b50a9e39ebdeef730909`:**
> Which of the given formulas of PL is the best symbolization of the following sentence?
> Either Britany painting spontaneously is a necessary condition for her fingers being stained with ink, or Debra is skeptical of others' intentions if and only if she is socializing.
> A. (P ⊃ I) ∨ (D ≡ S) … Answer: C

## The actual eval (MMLU formal_logic, 126 test items)

Same instruction preamble, **different argument**:
> mmlu_formal_logic-test-3: Construct a complete truth table for the following argument. Then, using the truth table, determine whether the argument is valid or invalid. If the argument is invalid, choose an option which presents a counterexample. (There may be other counterexamples as well.)
> ~G ⊃ H
> ~H / G
> A. Valid  B. Invalid. Counterexample when G and H are true  …

## What is actually "contaminated" (the matched span)

Only the **instruction preamble** and the **option phrasing**, both of which are verbatim-identical across MMLU items and therefore fully in the bloom:

- `"Construct a complete truth table for the following argument. Then, using the truth table, determine whether the argument is valid or invalid. If the argument is invalid, choose an option which presents a counterexample."` — ~40 words → dozens of 13-grams, all bloom hits → that paragraph scores 1.0 on its own.
- `"Invalid. Counterexample when … is true"` option boilerplate.

The **logical content** (the actual argument / the actual sentence to symbolize / the answer) is *not* in the eval.

## Evidence

Ran over the eval (126 items) and all 172,554 flagged docs:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| flagged doc #1's specific argument (`M ∨ O … M ∧ I`) present in eval | **0** |
| flagged doc #2's specific sentence (`Britany…`) present in eval | **0** |
| eval items using the "truth table" template | 15 / 126 |
| eval items using the "best symbolization" template | 17 / 126 |
| flagged docs containing a verbatim MMLU instruction template | **114,454 (66%)** |
| flagged docs containing the "Counterexample when" option boilerplate | 95,476 (55%) |

So this is a synthetic source that generates novel formal-logic MCQs *in MMLU's format*, and decon flags essentially all of them on the shared instruction template.

## Implication

This is a **third**, distinct false-positive class, on top of the shared-source-material one (code2text, books):

1. shared upstream material — public code / public books (code2text, Gutenberg, …)
2. coincidental phrase collisions (swde, mrpc on code)
3. **instruction-template / format collisions on templated synthetic data** — the largest single flag total in the whole run (172K docs)

Class 3 likely also inflates other high-flag templated-synthetic sources (`nemotron_sft/sft_math` 0.49%, `nemotron_specialized/math_textbooks` 0.45%), and it overlaps the templated-data hazard in #6851. Fixing it needs more than eval-set curation: either strip/normalize benchmark instruction templates before hashing, require the *answer* (not just the prompt template) to overlap, or exclude fixed-instruction MCQ benchmarks (MMLU-style) from paragraph-overlap matching. Net effect: the earlier "formal_logic is genuine contamination" line should be read as "formal_logic is the run's biggest false positive."

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 Started a data-driven pass here with a decon-specific viewer (single-page HTML report: per-source flag rates + sampled flagged docs with `matched_hashes → eval_hash_index → family` attribution) and ran the datakit **testbed samples** through decon (115 sources; finetranslations + ghalogs excluded).

**100M smoke** — small (21 flags total, 104/115 sources at 0; per-source samples are tiny at 100M), but the flagged-doc classification is clean and matches this issue's mechanisms. Reading them verbatim:

**Cluster B (reading-comprehension passages) is the top FP in the testbed**
- `hplt_v3` / `nemotron_cc_v2/medium_quality` → **anli_r3** (×6): every hit is an **AP news article** (Schladming ski injury, NHS cyberattack, Roger Ailes obit, EU financial-transaction tax). ANLI-r3 premises are news, so ordinary syndicated news in the web corpus matches the indexed premise.
- `nemotron_cc_v2/diverse_qa` → **race** (overlap **1.000**, 56 ngrams): the doc *is* a RACE reading passage.
- `nemotron_sft/sft_general` → **coqa** (0.97, 170 ngrams): a CoQA story ("One sunny May afternoon, a group of teenagers ditched school…").
- `nemotron_cc_v2/medium_quality` → **triviaqa** (0.59, 17 ngrams).

Root cause confirmed in code: LMH eval text = `doc_to_text` (prompt **incl. passage**) + `doc_to_target` + `_concat_strings(doc)` (**every raw field → passage again**), so passages get indexed twice — `prepare_eval_corpus.py:444-464`.

**Cluster D / coincidental**
- `nemotron_cc_math_v1/3` → `num_theory`: "MetaNumbers: 82,490 … composite number following 82,489" — numeric-sequence collision.
- `cais/hle` on a Spanish OMRON manual / telescope list / French policy article — coincidental prose 13-gram collisions (HLE is already Q+A-indexed).

Open question I'll settle on 100B: whether `anli_r3` is best treated as **B** (index Q+A, drop passage) or **A** (news-premise NLI = answerless corpus material → exclude).

Next: 100B run (in progress) for real FP volume, then A/B/D one at a time with before/after per-source compares + regression tests. Tooling/plan under `.agents/projects/decon-precision/`.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 Built a **recall harness** (`experiments/datakit/decontam/ops/recall_test.py`) and ran it to quantify the recall side directly: build a bloom over a sample of the staged eval corpus (80 tasks, 42,562 indexable items), inject 300 real eval items into synthetic corpus docs in four forms, mark them, measure the flag rate.

| injection form | recall |
|---|---|
| verbatim | **100.0%** |
| verbatim as its own paragraph among filler | **100.0%** |
| short-line-wrapped (re-wrapped to 8-word lines) | **0.0%** |
| embedded in same-paragraph filler (1×) | **29.7%** |

So the algorithm is **precision-favoring / verbatim-oriented**: it reliably catches verbatim benchmark text (even as one paragraph among many), but short-line contamination (MMLU/ARC options, tables, poetry — anything wrapped below the 13-token ngram window) is **completely invisible**, and embedded contamination is mostly diluted below the 0.5 paragraph-overlap threshold. This reproduces the recall cost described at the top of this issue with concrete numbers, and gives us a regression tripwire for any algorithm change.

(Precision-side fixes in progress: cluster D shipped — no-alphabetic-char ngram filter + cache versioning, tests green; cluster B implemented — index eval question+answer not the reading-comprehension passage, unit-tested; data-validation on the testbed samples next.)

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 **Cluster B fix validated on real reading-comprehension data** (`ops/b_validate.py`, controlled before/after). For each RC dataset I build two blooms — BASELINE (old eval text: rendered prompt incl. passage + target + all raw fields) vs FIXED (index question+answer only, passage dropped) — and measure over 300 real docs each: (a) does a **passage-only** corpus doc flag [the FP], (b) does a **question+answer** corpus doc flag [genuine-leakage recall].

| task | passage-only FP (base→fixed) | Q+A leakage recall (base→fixed) |
|---|---|---|
| anli_r3 | 300/300 → **1/300** | 203/300 → **203/300** |
| race | 300/300 → **0/300** | 94/300 → **94/300** |
| boolq | 300/300 → **0/300** | 1/300 → **1/300** |
| squad_v2 | 300/300 → **0/300** | 57/300 → **57/300** |

- **FP eliminated**: a corpus doc containing just the public passage flagged 100% before, ~0% after.
- **Recall preserved exactly**: Q+A leakage detection is unchanged (base == fixed) — the fix loses no genuine-contamination signal; it only stops indexing the public passage.

(boolq's low absolute recall is inherent — its answer is yes/no, so the distinctive Q+A is short; the fix doesn't change it. anli's residual 1/300 is a coincidental match.)

Fix: `prepare_eval_corpus._lmh_doc_text` drops passage-bearing fields (article/passage/premise/context/story/…) + `doc_to_text` (which renders them) for docs that carry a passage field, keeping question+answer+options. General (field-name based), unit-tested, and validated on real data here.

Alongside: **cluster D** (no-alphabetic-char ngram filter + cache-version) and **cluster A** (added `wikitext` + `lambada_*` — answerless perplexity/cloze over public text — to the read-time exclusion) are in, with `tests/datakit/test_decon.py` + `tests/datakit/decontam/test_prepare_eval_corpus.py` = 39 passed.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 **Post-fix full 100M run — cluster B verified, no collateral damage**

Regenerated the eval corpus with the cluster-B policy (drop the public RC passage from the indexed eval text, keep Q+A), rebuilt the bloom (36.3M n-gram rows, cluster-D letterless-ngram drop also applied), and re-ran the full 100M testbed decon over all 115 sources.

Flag comparison (same corpus, same 103,848 docs — no data loss):

| run | flags | removed |
|---|---|---|
| baseline (pre-B, D+A already in) | 14 | — |
| post-fix (B applied) | **6** | 8 |

The 8 flags that disappeared are **exactly** the RC-passage false positives B targets:

- `hplt_v3`: 4× `anli_r3`
- `nemotron_cc_v2/medium_quality`: 2× `anli_r3`
- `nemotron_sft/sft_general`: 1× `coqa`
- `nemotron_cc_v2/diverse_qa`: 1× `race`

The 6 that **remain** are all non-B and expected to stay — verbatim math problems (`hendrycks_math_*` / `minerva_math_*`), the `mmlu_formal_logic` truth-table template (cluster C, intentionally out of scope), a `cais/hle` overlap, and a `triviaqa` famous-quote ("Four score and seven years ago…"). No legitimate/other-cluster flag was touched.

Reports (GCS TTL): `gs://marin-eu-west4/tmp/ttl/rav/decon/decon_100m_postfix.html` (single run, with matched eval text) and `decon_100m_compare.html` (baseline→post-fix Δ).

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 **Correction on the remaining 6 flags — they are all false positives, not true contamination**

My previous comment called the 6 remaining post-B flags "verbatim math problems". That was wrong. Inspecting the *literal overlapping 13-grams* (not the per-eval attribution, which is misleading — one n-gram recurs across dozens of eval records, so the report was surfacing an arbitrary, unrelated eval problem) shows all 6 are false positives on shared boilerplate:

| source | actual overlapping 13-gram | FP mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `formal_logic` | `Construct a complete truth table for the following argument. Then, using the truth…` | **cluster C** instruction template (out of scope) |
| `sft_general` | `\frac{11 \times 10 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7}{5 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1}` | shared LaTeX arithmetic — both problems reduce to C(11,5); *different* problems |
| `sft_math` | `y^3 + z^3 - 3xyz = (x + y + z)(x^2 + y^2 + z^2 - xy…` | standard sum-of-cubes factoring identity |
| `4plus_mind` | `\frac{\tan A + \tan B}{1 - \tan A \tan B}` | standard tangent-addition identity |
| `triviaqa` | `Four score and seven years ago our fathers brought forth on this continent…` | famous quote embedded in the eval *question* (cluster-A-like) |
| `cais/hle` | `Apply a CNOT gate with the first qubit as control and the second…` | standard quantum-computing instruction phrase |

Net at 100M: effectively **zero true positives, 6 FPs** — and none are A/B/D. Four are coincidental overlaps on standard math/technical boilerplate (LaTeX identities, canonical instructions); one is cluster C; one is a famous quote in an eval question. The cluster-D letter filter can't catch the LaTeX-formula ones (they contain letters), so *shared standard formulas/identities in math corpora* is the next precision frontier if we want to push further — out of scope for the A/B/D PR, noted here for follow-up.

The viewer now displays the literal overlapping 13-gram per flagged doc (the honest doc∩eval evidence), so flags are self-explanatory rather than attributed to a cherry-picked unrelated eval record.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 status from #7051 — one of the two recall failure modes here is fixed; the other remains this issue's open scope.

**short-line contamination: fixed.** decon now splits paragraphs on `\n\n` (true paragraph) instead of every `\n` (`NGramConfig.paragraph_delimiter` default flipped in #7051). A hard-wrapped eval item is no longer a stack of sub-13-word lines — it rejoins into one matchable paragraph. Measured on the new labeled benchmark (`experiments/datakit/decontam/ops/contam_benchmark.py`), same corpus/seed, bloom rebuilt per delimiter:

| injection form | `\n` (old) | `\n\n` (new) |
|---|---|---|
| short-line-wrapped | 0.00 | **0.96** |
| verbatim / own-paragraph | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| inline-embedded | 0.35 | 0.37 |

overall recall `0.588 → 0.833` from the delimiter alone.

**embedded/inline contamination: still open — this issue's remaining scope.** an eval item inlined mid-paragraph among filler is still a minority of that (now larger) paragraph's 13-grams, so it stays below the 0.5 threshold — recall only `0.35 → 0.37`. This is inherent to per-paragraph fraction overlap and needs one of the matcher changes listed in the issue body (short-paragraph sliding window with a min length, length-normalization, or an absolute matched-hit-count path) rather than a delimiter tweak. Leaving this issue open for that.

separately, the precision/false-positive side of the decon work (FP clusters A/B/D + the per-source DF filter) shipped in #7051; the residual *cross-source* boilerplate FPs are now tracked in #7126.

comments.author: bethehand
comments.body:
Here is a real case for this issue's open recall scope, from the hero run (#9874). The document that contaminated Paloma PTB is a GitHub repo dump, `quanpn90/torch-nplm`. Its `data/ptb/valid.6grams` holds the whole PTB validation set as sliding 6-word windows, one per line. If Paloma PTB were indexed (today it isn't), the current matcher would score this document at overlap 0.000.

**Setup**
- Ran the matching functions from `lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/decon.py` (main, Oct 7) unchanged, with the `reference_pipeline.py` settings: 13-grams, `overlap_threshold=0.5`, `min_matched_features=2`, `\n\n` paragraphs.
- Rendered the repo the way `stack_v3.row_to_doc` does.
- Built the eval side from PTB `valid.txt`, which matches the start of Paloma's `ptb` doc as quoted in #9874.

| Training document | Max overlap | Flagged |
|---|---|---|
| torch-nplm as trained (6-gram windows) | 0.000 | no |
| the same repo plus the raw `data/ptb/valid.txt` | 1.000 | yes |
| the validation set as windows of any width from 3 to 30 | ≤ 0.144 | no |

The `\n\n` delimiter from #7051 doesn't help here. Each 13-gram in the paragraph runs across two or three overlapping windows, so it never matches the original text. Wider windows don't flag either. Only 13-grams that sit inside one line can match; those that cross a line break can't, and at sentence starts the windows are padded with `<s>`. Overlap peaks at 0.144, at width 24.

**Possible fix**

This follows the "sliding-window path" option in the issue body:
- Add a pre-pass that finds paragraphs whose lines are mostly shift-by-one windows (`line[i+1][:-1] == line[i][1:]`).
- Stitch those lines back into running text, drop padding tokens, and score the result as one more paragraph.

On this document:
- Overlap goes back to 1.000. With the PII scrubber's `<NAME>` substituted for `marvin davis`, it is 0.999.
- The stitched text reproduces the validation set token for token.
- The pass costs about 6% of the matcher's time.

On 5,724 ordinary files (the Marin repo and the CPython 3.12 standard library), it triggered on 0 of 241,449 paragraphs. It only fires on windowed layouts. When it fires, it scores the text the windows were cut from, so it shouldn't add a new kind of false positive.

Script and output: [decon_recall_windowed.py](https://github.com/bethehand/marin-hero-forecast/blob/main/eval-audit/code/decon_recall_windowed.py), [decon_recall_windowed.json](https://github.com/bethehand/marin-hero-forecast/blob/main/eval-audit/results/decon/decon_recall_windowed.json). I can turn this into a PR with a test in `tests/datakit/test_decon.py` if that's useful.

spillover_issues.author: ihodes
spillover_issues.body:
## Goal

Select and implement a pinned, open, text-only validation suite that approximates the capabilities in the current Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index across Marin pretraining, mid-training, and post-training checkpoints.

This is the concrete successor to #6050 and the eval-selection workstream under #6503. It is a **generative validation suite for both base/pretraining and post-trained checkpoints**, complementary to the lightweight PPL competency proxies in #5819. Benchmark items must remain isolated from training data, while results should be available alongside regular pretraining validation dashboards.

The suite is a proxy, not a reproduction of Artificial Analysis: several AA datasets and grading harnesses are private, and agentic behavior cannot be faithfully reduced to text-only tasks.

## Proposed benchmark mapping

| AA benchmark | Open text-only replacement | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **GDPval-AA v2** | **FinanceBench + IFBench + DS-1000** | Composite proxy for professional analysis, constraint-following, and practical technical work. There is no good single text-only equivalent for GDPval's agentic knowledge work and file outputs. |
| **τ³-Banking** | **τ²-Bench-Verified Retail** | Closest match for stateful customer-service workflows, policy adherence, and tool use. Use **BFCL** only as an easier, weaker fallback. |
| **Terminal-Bench v2.1** | **OT-TBench-Lite** | Direct lightweight terminal-agent proxy. |
| **SciCode** | **DS-1000 + CruxEval** | DS-1000 covers practical scientific/data coding; CruxEval adds code-execution reasoning. |
| **Humanity's Last Exam** | **MMLU-Pro + OlympiadBench Math** | MMLU-Pro supplies broad coverage; OlympiadBench supplies the hard tail. |
| **GPQA Diamond** | **MMLU-Pro science subset** | Easy to run but weaker than GPQA. Retaining open **GPQA Diamond** itself is the more faithful option if contamination policy permits. |
| **CritPt** | **OlympiadBench Physics** | Best simple open physics proxy, though exam-level rather than research-level. |
| **AA-Omniscience** | **Open factual QA with abstention and negative marking** | Use a SimpleQA-style or TriviaQA-derived held-out set; score correct `+1`, abstain `0`, incorrect `−1`. Report accuracy and hallucination rate separately as well as the signed score. |
| **AA-LCR** | **MRCR** | Good open long-context proxy, though more retrieval-oriented than AA-LCR's document synthesis. Cover the intended 10K–100K-token range. |

Artificial Analysis methodology: https://artificialanalysis.ai/methodology/intelligence-benchmarking

## Scoring proposal

- Preserve the current AA component weights so the proxy has a stable composite: GDPval proxy 20%, τ³ proxy 14%, Terminal proxy 16%, SciCode proxy 8%, HLE proxy 12%, GPQA proxy 6%, CritPt proxy 6%, Omniscience proxy 12%, and LCR proxy 6%.
- For composite replacements, normalize each constituent metric and macro-average within the component before applying the component weight.
- Publish every component score alongside the aggregate. Call the aggregate **Marin AA-II proxy**, never an AA score.
- Treat the weights and task revisions as a versioned configuration so the suite remains reproducible when AA or upstream benchmarks change.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Confirm dataset availability, licenses, canonical splits, and exact benchmark variants; pin dataset and harness revisions.
- [ ] Add explicit eval-only manifests and contamination metadata. No benchmark test item may enter training or core PPL tracking, consistent with #5819.
- [ ] Implement each component behind Marin's standard OpenAI-compatible eval entrypoint and make the suite selectable by one versioned config in #6503.
- [ ] Pin prompts/chat templates, decoding parameters, parsers/graders, seeds, repeats, tokenizer/model revisions, and context lengths.
- [ ] Emit raw per-item outputs plus component metrics, confidence intervals, runtime/cost, failure counts, and the versioned composite score.
- [ ] Provide a tiny deterministic smoke subset for scheduled regression testing, plus the full-suite path.
- [ ] Run a representative model panel and measure repeatability and rank correlation against available AA/Harbor component results. Document where the text-only proxy fails to preserve rankings.
- [ ] Publish results through the eval results/leaderboard path tracked by #6043 and #6503.
- [ ] Document how to add, replace, or retire a component without silently changing historical scores.

## Related work

- #6050 — original AA-II eval TBD (closed in favor of July work)
- #6503 — automated eval system parent Epic
- #6863 — July Evalchemy/Harbor execution work
- #5819 — lightweight PPL proxies for AA-measured competencies; complementary to this generative checkpoint suite
- #7090 — broader new-evals wish-list, including scalable proxies for several AA components

| SciCode | CruxEval | [facebookresearch/cruxeval](https://github.com/facebookresearch/cruxeval) | MIT | Execution pass@1 for input/output prediction |
| HLE breadth | MMLU-Pro non-science categories | [TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro](https://huggingface.co/datasets/TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro) | MIT | Gold multiple-choice accuracy |
| HLE hard math tail | OlympiadBench Math, English text-only open-ended subset | [OpenBMB/OlympiadBench](https://github.com/OpenBMB/OlympiadBench) | MIT in GitHub; Apache 2.0 in Hugging Face metadata | Exact, numeric, or symbolic answer accuracy |
| GPQA scientific reasoning | MMLU-Pro biology, chemistry, and physics categories | [TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro](https://huggingface.co/datasets/TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro) | MIT | Gold multiple-choice accuracy |
| CritPt physics | OlympiadBench Physics, English text-only open-ended subset | [OpenBMB/OlympiadBench](https://github.com/OpenBMB/OlympiadBench) | MIT in GitHub; Apache 2.0 in Hugging Face metadata | Exact, numeric, or symbolic answer accuracy |
| Omniscience | SimpleQA | [OpenAI simple-evals](https://github.com/openai/simple-evals) | MIT | Deterministic normalized gold match with correct `+1`, abstain `0`, incorrect `-1`; reference-answer conditional loss/PPL for base checkpoints |

FinanceBench, TriviaQA, BFCL, GPQA Diamond, and direct AA datasets are out of scope. MMLU-Pro is partitioned so the HLE and GPQA proxies do not score the same questions twice. Reference-answer conditional loss/PPL is an auxiliary base-checkpoint metric; generated-answer accuracy remains the post-training metric.

The first definition-of-done item remains open until the exact dataset and harness revisions, splits, and OlympiadBench configurations are pinned.

spillover_issues.author: wmoss
spillover_issues.body:
Currently to set Zephyr to run with the `InlineRunner` requires passing it in to `ZephyrContext`. The `ZephyrContext` is usually created in shared code (e.g. `lib/marin/src/marin/processing/classification/deduplication/exact.py`). It would be nice to be able to set this per-run.

Options I can think of off the cuff,
1. Command line parameter (plumbed through to `ZephyrContext`)
2. Environment variable (but I sort of hate these)

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue, AGENTS.md, fix-issue/pull-request skills
- [x] Locate `ZephyrContext` definition and all call sites
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (no overlapping PRs/issues)
- [x] Post research + proposed approach
- [ ] Await human direction on which option to take before implementing

# Research

`ZephyrContext.stage_runner_factory` is the only knob to swap `InlineRunner` ↔ `SubprocessRunner`. The default is picked by `_default_stage_runner_factory_for(client)` in `__post_init__`: `LocalClient` → `InlineRunner`, distributed → `SubprocessRunner`. There are ~30 production call sites that construct `ZephyrContext(...)` (deduplication, tokenize, datakit/download, classification), so changing the runner today means editing whichever shared module owns the construction.

**Relevant code**
- [\`execution.py#L1658-L1739\`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/zephyr/src/zephyr/execution.py#L1658-L1739) — \`ZephyrContext\` + \`__post_init__\`
- [\`execution.py#L329-L348\`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/zephyr/src/zephyr/execution.py#L329-L348) — default factory selection
- [\`execution.py#L1718-L1726\`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/zephyr/src/zephyr/execution.py#L1718-L1726) — existing \`ZEPHYR_MAX_WORKERS\` env precedent
- [\`runners.py\`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/zephyr/src/zephyr/runners.py) — \`InlineRunner\` / \`SubprocessRunner\`
- [\`exact.py#L78-L85\`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/processing/classification/deduplication/exact.py#L78-L85) — representative shared-code construction

# Proposed Fix

Two viable options; both keep an explicit \`stage_runner_factory=...\` kwarg as the highest-priority override.

**Option A — env var \`ZEPHYR_STAGE_RUNNER=inline|subprocess\`** (~30 lines, self-contained in \`execution.py\` + a test). Reads in \`__post_init__\` only when \`stage_runner_factory is None\`. Mirrors the existing \`ZEPHYR_MAX_WORKERS\` pattern, requires zero call-site changes, lets \`ZEPHYR_STAGE_RUNNER=inline uv run ...\` flip the runner per-invocation. Downsides: AGENTS.md flags env-vars-over-explicit-params as a pitfall, and the issue notes \"I sort of hate these.\"

**Option B — command-line / config plumbing.** Add \`stage_runner: Literal[\"inline\", \"subprocess\"] | None\` to each shared entry point (\`dedup_exact_*\`, \`fuzzy_*\`, \`tokenize\`, datakit downloaders, etc.) and forward into \`ZephyrContext\`. ~30 callsites to update plus the public CLI configs that wrap them. Cleaner per AGENTS.md, but a multi-module change well over the 100-line bar — needs a design pass on which entry points actually need it and what the parameter name should be.

I lean toward Option A as the minimally-disruptive fix: it solves the stated pain (no editing shared code to flip a runner) without churning every dedup/tokenize/download module, and the env var is opt-in (default behavior unchanged). Happy to implement Option B instead, or a hybrid (env var now + plumb through specific high-traffic entry points later).

Which would you like? Holding off on a PR until you confirm.
